p5_b0.ocr: The data presents a demographic breakdown by age group and gender as well as various mechanisms for delivering financial aid.

p5_b1.ocr: In the age group of 35–44 years, there are 1 Female and 1 Male; in the 45–54 years age group, there are 1 Female and 15 Males; in the 55–64 years category, there are 6 Females and 28 Males; in the 65–74 years group, there are 6 Females and 55 Males; and finally, in the 75–84 years category, there is 1 Female and 1 Male.

p5_b3.ocr: The mechanisms of financial aid include Output-Based Aid (OBA), which is defined as a results-based mechanism that is used to deliver basic infrastructure and social services to the poor, and it is excluded for use predominantly outside of the health sector.

p5_b4.ocr: Cash on Delivery (COD) is defined as a mechanism that gives recipients full responsibility and authority over funds paid in proportion to verified measures of progress toward a single specific outcome, but it is excluded due to political difficulty in the agent having complete control. Performance-Based Financing (PBF) is defined as fee-for-service paid to providers conditional on specific predefined indicators for degree and/or quality, and it is included for use in the health sector and political feasibility.

p5_b5.ocr:
Mechanism Definition Inclusion/Exclusion criteria
Output-Based Aid (OBA) A results-based mechanism that is used to deliver basic infrastructure and social services to the poor Excluded for use predominantly outside of the health sector
Cash on Delivery (COD) A mechanism that gives recipients full responsibility and authority over funds paid in proportion to verified measures of progress toward a single specific outcome Excluded for political difficulty in agent having complete control
Performance-Based Financing (PBF) Fee-for-service paid to providers conditional on specific predefined indicators for degree and/or quality Included for use in health sector and political feasibility
Performance-Based Contracting (PBC) A fixed price for an output or outcome with a variable increase/decrease in payment based on performance, typically applied to NGOs Included for use in health sector and political feasibility
Conditional Cash Transfers (CCTs) A demand-side mechanism that provides incentives directly to program beneficiaries Included for use in health sector and political feasibility

p5_b6.ocr: Performance-Based Contracting (PBC) is a fixed price for an output or outcome with a variable increase/decrease in payment based on performance, included for use in health sector and political feasibility.

p5_b7.ocr: Conditional Cash Transfers (CCTs) is defined as a demand-side mechanism that provides incentives directly to program beneficiaries, also included for use in health sector and political feasibility.
